subject: Cooking
title: Natto: The Ferment People Love to Hate
description: A micro-lesson that makes Natto: The Ferment People Love to Hate usable.

hook.text: Natto is fermented soybeans that smell like old gym socks and stretch into sticky, slimy threads. Millions love it.

buildup.text: Bacillus subtilis bacteria ferment soybeans for 24 hours, producing a pungent, ammonia-rich aroma.

discovery.text: Natto contains nattokinase — an enzyme that dissolves blood clots, studied as a natural cardiovascular aid.

twist.text: It's also the richest food source of vitamin K2, which directs calcium into bones instead of arteries.

climax.text: Japanese regions with high natto consumption have measurably lower rates of heart disease and osteoporosis.

punchline.text: The food that repels most foreigners might be the healthiest ferment on Earth.

quiz.question: What unique enzyme does natto contain?

details.summary: Natto is Japanese fermented soybeans with an intensely pungent smell and sticky, stringy texture caused by Bacillus subtilis bacteria. Despite its challenging sensory profile, natto is extremely nutritious, containing nattokinase enzyme and high levels of vitamin K2 and protein.
details.whyItMatters: Natto is one of fermentation's most extreme products. Its polarizing nature illustrates how cultural familiarity shapes food acceptance and how fermentation creates unique nutritional compounds.
takeaways: Bacillus subtilis bacteria create natto's stringy, sticky texture
Nattokinase enzyme may help break down blood clots
Natto is one of the richest food sources of vitamin K2

faq.question: Why is natto so slimy and strong-smelling?
faq.answer: Bacillus subtilis produces polyglutamic acid, which forms the characteristic sticky strings. The bacteria also produce pyrazines and ammonia compounds responsible for the pungent smell. These are the same compounds that make natto nutritionally unique.

faq.question: How do Japanese people typically eat natto?
faq.answer: Natto is most commonly eaten at breakfast over hot rice with soy sauce, mustard, and chopped green onions. Vigorous stirring before eating increases the stringiness, which is considered desirable. Some people add raw egg. It is an everyday food, not a delicacy.
